core.title: Make every mutating request declared in markup signal that it is in flight
core.given: An element in markup issues a mutating request through one of the stack's declarative request constructs that change server state, so a duplicate is not harmless.
core.when: That element exists in the markup.
core.then: The element issuing the mutation declares an in-flight progress signal: at least one of the stack's progress-signal constructs (either one satisfies; declaring more than one is fine).
prefer: A signal that disables the issuing control for the duration of the request, making a double submit physically impossible, where a duplicate would be expensive.
A signal that shows a busy region for the duration of the request, so the user can see that something is happening.
avoid: A mutating element with no signal at all — invisible while in flight.
A visibility-only signal where duplicates are expensive: it tells the user to wait but does not stop them.
Treating a server-side idempotency key as an exemption from the rule: a real mitigation, but one the rule cannot see.
Adding progress signals to elements that issue only idempotent read requests under this rule — a UX preference, out of scope.
unless: The element issues only an idempotent (read) request — a duplicate is harmless.
core.why: In-place fragment updates replace content without navigation, so the page looks identical while the request is in flight (full-page navigation used to give a free progress signal); users correctly read 'nothing happened', click again, and a non-idempotent request runs twice (duplicate orders, charges, rows).
evidence: The stack's markup check reports no finding across the in-scope markup.
Every markup element (opening tag) declaring one of the stack's mutating request constructs also declares at least one of its progress-signal constructs.
verification: A markup scan finds every element declaring one of the stack's mutating request constructs and flags the element when it declares none of the stack's progress-signal constructs; findings are deduplicated per element (an element carrying several mutating constructs reports once).
Idempotent read constructs are not scoped: an element declaring at least one progress signal passes; only an element declaring none is a violation.

The check scans all in-scope markup of the kinds the profile counts as markup — standalone markup files, templates, and markup embedded in source files — not only changed lines, so pre-existing violations and signals removed from still-mutating elements are covered. Which trees are in scope and which are never scanned is the stack's single scan scope and exclusion list, owned by the checker; this rule adds no exclusions of its own.
Server-driven idempotency (an idempotency key at the endpoint) is a real mitigation but invisible to the check; it does not exempt the element from signalling progress to the user.
Per-rule enforcement (not a profile fact): severity 3, disposition strict — every finding fails the run; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: a markup element issuing a mutating request declares no progress signal
markup containing one of the stack's mutating request constructs is touched, including removal of a progress signal from an element that still issues a mutating request

fires: Any markup element, new or pre-existing, declares one of the stack's mutating request constructs and none of its progress-signal constructs.
An element's request construct changes from an idempotent read construct to a mutating construct, with no progress signal.
A progress signal is removed from an element that still issues a mutating request.
A mutating element without a signal lives in markup embedded in a template or in a source file rather than in a standalone markup file.
doesNotFire: An element issuing only an idempotent read request.
A mutating element that declares at least one progress signal.

profileRequirements.meaning: The declarative markup construct that issues a destructive (mutating) request; together with idiom.mutation_requests it forms the mutating set this rule scopes.

The declarative markup constructs that issue non-destructive mutating requests; together with idiom.destructive_request they form the mutating set this rule scopes (bun.json treats the four verbs as one set).

The declarative markup constructs that satisfy the obligation by signalling that a request is in flight (a busy-indicator region or disabling the issuing control); any one satisfies, several are fine.
profileRequirements.bunValue: hx-indicator or hx-disabled-elt (either satisfies; both is fine)

profileRequirements.meaning: Which artifact kinds count as markup in which the mutating request constructs and progress signals are looked for; the rule applies wherever such markup appears, with no file-kind restriction.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Applies to htmx markup wherever it appears (HTML files, templates, or markup embedded in source files); no file-kind restriction.

bunOnly.text: hx-disabled-elt (disables the control in flight, making double-submit impossible) where a duplicate is expensive, e.g. <form hx-post="…" hx-disabled-elt="find button">.
bunOnly.reason: Concrete markup example naming the stack's constructs; per rule 4 the core keeps the role-level pattern (a disabling signal) and bun.json itself is the delivered reference example.

bunOnly.text: hx-indicator (spinner region in flight) to show something is happening, e.g. <form hx-post="…" hx-indicator="#spinner">.
bunOnly.reason: Concrete markup example naming the stack's constructs; the core keeps the role-level pattern (a busy-region signal).

bunOnly.text: <form hx-post="…">…</form> with no signal — invisible in flight.
bunOnly.reason: Concrete snippet in the stack's markup dialect; the core keeps the neutral pattern (a mutating element with no signal).

bunOnly.text: htmx_hypermedia_detector reports no finding across the in-scope markup.
bunOnly.reason: Detector and finding ids of this rule are realization details (vocabulary notProfileKeys); the core's verification names the check generically.

bunOnly.text: Zero-dependency Bun detector: find each mutating verb attribute (hx-post, hx-put, hx-patch, hx-delete), extract the enclosing opening tag, flag the element when it declares neither hx-indicator nor hx-disabled-elt.
bunOnly.reason: Names the runtime (Bun), the concrete attributes, and this rule's detector implementation; realization detail. The core describes the same check generically over the profile's construct lists.
The hypermedia dialect name and the workspace id are stack facts with no neutral equivalent; the core triggers on the markup file kind, which idiom.markup_kinds expands.

bunOnly.text: htmx_hypermedia_detector: element with hx-post|hx-put|hx-patch|hx-delete declaring neither hx-indicator nor hx-disabled-elt
bunOnly.reason: The detector id and concrete attribute names are realization details; the core keeps the finding shape generic over the profile's construct lists.

classification.note: The semantic definition (changes server state, duplicate not harmless) is core; the concrete verb list is the union of the two profile keys (hx-delete + hx-post/hx-put/hx-patch = the four verbs bun.json scopes).
Already stack-neutral; kept verbatim.

'htmx swaps fragments in place' generalized to in-place fragment updates without naming the framework; duplicate-consequence rationale kept in full.
Core prefers a disabling signal where a duplicate is expensive; the concrete construct (hx-disabled-elt) and snippet stay in the reference example.
Core prefers a busy-region signal; the concrete construct (hx-indicator) and snippet stay in the reference example.
Neutral pattern: a mutating element with no signal, invisible in flight; the concrete snippet is Bun-only.
Generalized to 'a visibility-only signal'; the named construct is carried by the profile key.

Kept semantic (idempotent read, duplicate harmless). The concrete read construct (hx-get) need not be identified by the check because only elements declaring mutating constructs are examined, so the exclusion falls out of the scoping.

Finding fact kept generically (mutating element with no signal, needs_new_observer, scans all in-scope markup not only the diff); the detector id is bunOnly.

Change fact neutralized over the profile's mutating request constructs: activation requires touched markup that contains a mutating request construct, which also covers removal of a progress signal from an element that still issues a mutating request. It does not independently activate on progress-signal constructs, exactly matching bun.json's change fact (touched markup containing hx-post|hx-put|hx-patch|hx-delete). Kept as an early-firing observer subordinate to the finding fact.

neutralityNotes: 1) bun.json scopes one mutating set of four verbs; the closed vocabulary expresses it only as the union of idiom.destructive_request (hx-delete) and idiom.mutation_requests (hx-post, hx-put, hx-patch). A single 'mutating requests' key was not proposed because it would near-duplicate idiom.mutation_requests; the union instantiates to exactly bun.json's four verbs. 2) idiom.markup#progress_signals is proposed: no existing key covers in-flight signalling. 3) The idempotent-read exclusion is kept semantic; no read-construct key is needed because the check only examines elements declaring mutating constructs, so reads are never flagged (bun.json's 'hx-get is not scoped' falls out of the scoping). 4) Severity 3 and strict disposition are per-rule and live in core:verification, not the profile. 5) bun.json never states the concrete scan scope ('the in-scope markup'), so the core defers scope and exclusions to the stack's single scan/exclusion list owned by the checker rather than naming trees. 6) The rationale is generalized from 'htmx swaps fragments in place' to in-place fragment updates without navigation; the framework name stays in the Bun realization. 7) The change activation fact fires only on touched markup containing a mutating request construct (per the profile's mutating construct keys); touching a progress-signal construct alone, on an element issuing no mutating request, does not activate — matching bun.json's change fact, whose condition is touched markup containing hx-post|hx-put|hx-patch|hx-delete, with signal removal covered only as removal from an element that still issues a mutating request.
